answer.evidence: The sprite is a full 48x48 square. Its width is 48 in every row, and it has a brown dirt border and speckled gray asphalt inside. The only depth cue is a small dirt hollow at rows 21-28, with a dark far-wall edge at row 21 and a lighter chipped rim at row 28. There is no vertical front face of 3 or more rows and no front-edge line with eave shadow beneath a top band. The whole thing reads as a flat plate seen from above, which fits a flat decal, though the opaque square fill is not a transparent decal.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine: 8 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for grass, 0% near-flat coverage, and only 13% neutral dark edge pixels, so the edges lean brown rather than black. The picture is weaker than the numbers. Only 10 distinct colours are used in total, so the ramps are shallow, about 4 steps on the asphalt and 3-4 on the pothole. The pothole is a small, muddy orange-brown patch. The far wall, shadow, dirt bottom, chipped lighter near rim and loose chips are not clearly separated. The asphalt is mostly speckle noise on a near-uniform grey-brown. It lacks the per-stone shading and highlight edges of the paving reference. It is not a flat fill, but it would look thinner and less crafted next to the Beodeul references, so I fail it when in doubt.
